market_name: Will 6 Fed rate cuts happen in 2026?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether 2y/10y Treasury yields are falling in tandem and if fed funds futures (SOFR/ZQ) confirm added cut pricing.
time_plan.1h: Confirm TLT move is holding and not a fake-out; watch for any Fed speaker or macro data driving it.
time_plan.2h: Assess whether move is broad-based (dollar, gold, rate futures all consistent) or isolated to the prediction market.
time_plan.6h: Re-evaluate against any scheduled data/headlines; check if dovish repricing persists into US session.
time_plan.12h: Mark final TLT return vs entry; note whether the prediction-market shift preceded or lagged the bond move.

predictions.reasoning: A sharp rise in the implied probability of 6 Fed cuts (150bps) in 2026 signals a much more dovish/easing path than currently priced, typically tied to expected economic weakness or emergency action. Falling policy-rate expectations pull front- and long-end yields lower, lifting duration-heavy TLT. This is the most direct, liquid mapping of a Fed-cut probability shift.

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check DXY direction and real-yield proxies (TIP) for confirmation.
time_plan.1h: Verify gold move aligns with falling yields rather than a risk-off spike from an unrelated shock.
time_plan.2h: Compare gold vs dollar to confirm the driver is rate expectations, not pure safe-haven flow.
time_plan.6h: Reassess against any macro releases and whether dovish narrative holds.
time_plan.12h: Record final GLD return and consistency with the Treasury signal.

predictions.reasoning: Aggressive expected easing lowers real yields and typically weakens the dollar, both supportive of gold. A jump in the 6-cut probability implies deeper cuts, reinforcing lower real-rate expectations. Gold is a liquid, broadly traded proxy that benefits from a dovish repricing.

evidence_used: Market question implies probability of 6 (150bps) Fed cuts in 2026
Fed-cut expectations map directly to Treasury yields, the dollar, and gold
Dovish repricing lowers yields (bond prices up) and real rates (gold up)
uncertainty_notes: Fed-cut probability shifts often reflect already-public data (CPI, jobs, FOMC speak), so leakage/edge may be minimal
6 cuts is an extreme dovish outcome usually tied to recession, which would be equity-negative and could complicate cross-asset signals
12h magnitude for these ETFs is far below the 700bps tradable threshold, so neither is 'tradable' by the stated rule

llm_justification.summary: A sharp increase in the implied probability of 6 Fed rate cuts in 2026 represents a dovish repricing of the policy path, most cleanly implying lower Treasury yields (TLT up) and a lower real-rate/dollar backdrop supportive of gold (GLD up). Both are liquid proxies but expected 12h moves are modest and well below the 700bps tradable bar, so this is a directional research signal, not a tradable one.
key_assumptions: The probability move reflects genuine dovish repricing, not noise or thin liquidity in the prediction market
Treasury yields and gold respond in the standard direction to lower expected policy rates
No offsetting shock (risk-off equity crash, inflation surprise) dominates the tape
failure_modes: The Fed-cut expectation change is already public (post-CPI/NFP/FOMC), so no informational edge and move is already priced
6-cut scenarios imply recession, which could steepen risk-off flows and muddle the clean rate-to-asset mapping
Prediction-market move reverses as thin-market mispricing rather than real information
ETF proxies (TLT, GLD) have muted 12h responses; magnitude far below the 700bps tradable threshold
Mislabeled topic ('military_conflict') suggests metadata noise; the market is macro/monetary, not geopolitical
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
